messages:
Lina: FYI getting multiple reports from APAC customers about a spike of 502/504s for small-embedding requests starting ~2024-11-18 09:02 UTC. Examples: request_id=apac-7a3c, apac-7a4d. Affected customers see retries and billing duplicates.

Omar: assigning to oncall, looking now. Do we have an incident?

ops-bot: Incident INC-2024-542 created (high, routing/ingress). Pager duty notified.

Kai: quick scan of ingress logs (ap-southeast-1) looks like connection resets and RST_STREAM on upstream to inference-pool nodes. Sample: 
```
[ingress][2024-11-18T09:03:12Z] req=apac-7a3c status=502 upstream_err="RST_STREAM" upstream_addr=10.12.34.56:443
[ingress][2024-11-18T09:03:12Z] conn_pool_exhausted=true idle_timeout_ms=60
```

Lina: repro steps from customer (they shared): small synchronous embed calls at high QPS (~300 rps) from a single NAT IP. They switched to SDK default and saw retries loop.

Paul: customer-facing: I told them we're investigating and recommended temporary SDK rate limit (max_concurrency=4) + exponential backoff. They asked if it's an APAC regional issue.

Omar: I'm seeing high ephemeral port reuse on egress NAT nodes for ap-southeast. Kernel tcp_state shows TIME_WAIT spikes and conn reuse. Looks like NAT pool hitting ephemeral exhaustion -> upstream connections dropped.

Kai: Repro locally with wrk against hosted endpoint using client IP binding simulating NAT fanout:
```
wrk -t8 -c120 -d30s --latency --script=small_embed.lua https://api.redwood-hosted.example/v1/embeddings
```
Result: ~25% 502/504, upstream RSTs, p95 latency spikes.

Lina: customer gave sample curl repro; posting redacted example:
```
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST -d '{"input":"short"}' https://api.redwood-hosted.example/v1/embeddings &
done; wait
```

Kai: Immediate mitigation candidates: 1) increase NAT ephemeral port pool on ap-southeast egress nodes, 2) bump LB idle timeout to avoid half-closed connection churn, 3) rate-limit aggressive clients at ingress (short-term).

Omar: I applied quick throttling rule to customer tenant to 150 rps and added SDK guidance to set max_concurrency=4/backoff=500ms. Also raised NAT ephemeral range on two egress VMs and restarted their nat-agent (rolling) — monitoring now.

Lina: Thanks. Customer confirmed retries dropped after applying their client-side throttle.

Kai: Observability: after NAT bump we see ephemeral ports utilization drop from 96% -> 40% and 5xx rate for the tenant down to 0.8% from 27% over 15m.

Omar: Rolling change to increase NAT pool and adjust LB idle timeout 60s -> 300s scheduled across ap-southeast edge fleet. Patch PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/PR-3492 (ingress: increase keepalive).

Paul: Sent customer status: "We identified NAT exhaustion on our APAC egress as root cause. Short-term mitigations applied (client throttle + SDK guidance). We're rolling a regional config change; we'll follow up once complete."

Lina: Postmortem notes to collect: exact customers impacted, SDK versions, client IP counts, retry patterns, billing duplicate exposure window. Also recommend adding server-side rate-limiter for tenant fanout to prevent single-IP NAT storms.

Omar: Monitoring/alert follow-ups: add alert for ephemeral port exhaustion >80% and 5xx rate >5% sustained 5m per region.

Kai: Closing loop: rollout finished at 2024-11-18T10:45 UTC, ap-southeast 5xxs returned to baseline. Will draft RCA for tomorrow's support sync.

Lina: Customer notified that region is back to normal and we will send postmortem. :thumbsup:

Paul: Customer asked for billing credit; I started a support ticket and flagged for CS review.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2024-542 resolved (status: mitigated).

Omar: Notes for follow-up: long term we should 1) implement tenant-level ingress smoothing, 2) document SDK best-practices for high-qps small requests, 3) evaluate NAT pool autoscaling for edge nodes.

Lina: Thanks everyone, closing thread unless new regressions reported.
